summary_html: Agency fails to **disclose required data or reports**, obstructing transparency. Federal statutes require public reporting under CAPTA, FOIA, and Sunshine provisions.
authority_html:
- **CAPTA (42 U.S.C. §§ 5101–5116)** — mandates public availability of child-fatality information  
- **Freedom of Information Act (5 U.S.C. § 552)** — public access to federal records  
- **Government in the Sunshine Act (5 U.S.C. § 552b)** — open-meeting requirements

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: Summary judgment applying collateral estoppel to a registry substantiation was reversed because the Human Services Board could not inspect the related CHINS file without a need-to-know designation from the family court under 33 V.S.A. § 5117(b)(1)(F), and the stipulated facts did not establish what the substantiation required.
key_cases.relevance: It identifies the statutory gate that controls transfer of confidential juvenile records between Vermont bodies.
key_cases.quote: A need-to-know designation from the family court was required before the Board could inspect the contents of the juvenile files in question.

key_cases.case_name: In re A.O. & I.O., Juveniles & In re B.G. & E.G., Juveniles
key_cases.holding: The CHINS merits and disposition orders for four children were reversed and vacated as unsupported by the findings or the record, and the orders allowing a party's advocate to inspect the other children's juvenile records without a need-to-know designation were reversed.
key_cases.relevance: The opinion reverses orders that released confidential juvenile records to a party's advocate without the statutory need-to-know designation.
key_cases.quote: We therefore reverse the CHINS merits determination as unsupported by the findings or the record.

key_cases.case_name: Toensing v. Attorney Gen. of Vt.
key_cases.holding: Records produced or acquired in the course of agency business are public records under the Public Records Act even when they sit in employees' private accounts, and where a requester specifically seeks such communications the agency must ask the named employees to produce them.
key_cases.relevance: It is the leading Vermont decision on an agency's search obligations under the Public Records Act and therefore on what counts as a disclosure failure.
key_cases.quote: the PRA's definition of "public record" includes digital documents stored in private accounts, but emphasize that it extends only to documents that otherwise meet the definition of public records

timeline_requirements.starts_from: Date the administrative reviewer sent notice of the decision on the substantiation review (33 V.S.A. § 4916a(i)); the review itself must be requested within 30 days after the Department sent notice of the right to review (33 V.S.A. § 4916a(c)(1))
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: If no review by the Human Services Board is requested, the Department's decision is final and the person has no further right of review under this section; the Board may grant a waiver upon good cause shown (33 V.S.A. § 4916b(d)).
